searchText: I'll definitely been wondering this myself, were you able to find an authoritative answer? Also wondering if theres a way to force eip-1559 tx's on dapps - perhaps intercepting the call to metamask? I am not 100% sure, but it seems that type0 txs gas price is automatically divided in current base fee + priority fee, regarding the speed of the validation For example, if I submit a type0 tx with gas price 100 gwei and the current base fee is 50 gwei, the tx is treated (comparing to type2 tx) as 50 gwei for base fee and 50 gwei for priority fee Old-style transactions with a gas price of 100 gwei are treated as having `max_fee_per_gas = max_priority_fee_per_gas = 100 Gwei` As long as the base fee is lower than 100 Gwei, the transaction is eligible for inclusion. Anyway, the base free dropped enough a few hours ago, so that queue has been cleared wait a moment you're telling me that the gas limit has a role in this too? Where do you see gas limit? max_fee = gas limit * gas price `max_fee_per_gas` not `max_fee` oh ok you meant the max gas price in jargon terms Yes, those are the two fields that type2 txs specify. And type 1 txs have those two fields set/converted like `max_fee_per_gas = max_priority_fee_per_gas = gasPrice` ok I think I understood it now, thanks! On the scope of the great rename I suggest the following for the "consensus" sub of Discord: merge <#595701053161209866> <#778633028451696680> <#823882674446794752>, (it is highly unlikely for someone following one not to follow all, and are so low volume that no one really will miss important messages with this move). Get rid of <#798403407076917269> last message is from April, so either a different forum with less interaction would work (magicians or research) or just merge in general. Same for the networking related channels like <#646778960830660623> <#595701087499976854> <#682024484689149955> <#710831784991916072> can be safely merged without anyone being spammed by the move or losing messages. I feel like there are a ton of these that can be made without really bugging the people that have something to say in those channels and helping the lurkers like me I'll let <@!291925846556540928> and <@!203220829473996800> make that change because they have much more context than me on consensus-layer stuff. <#692062809701482577> has been moved into the General... and I guess that means we should probably just rename it to #merge 😅 ohh, I'm not requesting these changes, just suggesting, I feel like there's a ton that can safely be merged. In the three main sections (general / Execution / Consensus) but just stick to consensus which I'm more comfortable (and mostly because those I follow 🙂 ). By the way, I think it would be better to have only three main setions instead of the current 5: it doesn't make sense to have a main board named Consensus R&D when the whole server is supposed to be R&D. I'd just stick to General/Execution/Consensus, although I understand that there's no consensus on the word "Consensus" Yeah, I'm fine with 3 vs. 5 sections. Curious- I’m mostly lurking and am new. I see a lot of fervor, genuine passion and excitement for development on ethereum- why is that? Are you all doing this in your free time or do most people here get paid by the ethereum foundation? most of the people here are not paid by the EF, no. a lot of people do work fulltime in the space, but for different companies. as well as a ton of enthusiasts working on things part time, or community members following along with upgrades. there's also an apprenticeship program with a bunch of participants all in all, people are here for their own reasons, but all generally interested in core Ethereum protocol development For the record, I find the separate <#710831784991916072> channel very helpful. It's low traffic but the traffic that is there is important and would likely get lost if it merged into a bigger channel. yeah, I'm keeping that as is merging the other networking ones though Yep that makes sense to me. Phenomenal. Thanks for the response! Great to see

excerpts.author: lanor
excerpts.content:
I am not 100% sure, but it seems that type0 txs gas price is automatically divided in current base fee + priority fee, regarding the speed of the validation
For example, if I submit a type0 tx with gas price 100 gwei and the current base fee is 50 gwei, the tx is treated (comparing to type2 tx) as 50 gwei for base fee and 50 gwei for priority fee

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: Old-style transactions with a gas price of 100 gwei are treated as having `max_fee_per_gas = max_priority_fee_per_gas = 100 Gwei`

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: As long as the base fee is lower than 100 Gwei, the transaction is eligible for inclusion.
